rawanswer_preserved.answer: Reputation range includes the display folder matching your reputation and all lower-numbered folders; folders map to reputation bands 1, 2–3, 4–6, 7–9, 10–12, 13–15. Reputation 10+ requires Cards II. At 15, each further reputation step gives 1 appeal. You may not look through the discard pile during the game.

source_summary_support.quote: **Reputation track and display:** whenever you increase reputation, advance your counter 1 step. Reaching a space with a bonus grants that bonus immediately, once. Reputation 10+ requires the upgraded Cards action (reminder icon on space 10 / folder 5). If your counter is on space 15 and you gain more reputation, it stays on 15 and you take **1 appeal per remaining reputation step**. "Within reputation range" = the display card on the folder matching your counter plus all lower-numbered folders. After a turn in which display cards were taken: move cards from higher-numbered folders down (keeping their order), then fill empty spaces from the deck. You may not look through the discard pile during the game.

rawanswer_preserved.answer: Build I builds exactly 1 building of size no greater than strength; Build II builds any number of different buildings with total size no greater than strength, never two identical in one action. Build on empty map spaces only, not beyond map or over buildings, water or rock. Restricted-icon spaces require Build II. New kiosks must be at least 3 spaces from every other kiosk. Each pavilion immediately gives +1 appeal once.

Unique buildings can never be built with this action — they only come into play via their Sponsor cards.

records.question: Which enclosures are available with Build I versus II; how many of each special enclosure; can Build create unique buildings; and what happens when the map is fully covered?
records.scope_decision: Both identify available types and one-per-special limits. Unrestricted covering every non-terrain space gives seven appeal applies regardless of effect source. Volunteered four-tile supply quantities are explicitly supported.

rawanswer_preserved.answer: Build I permits standard enclosures, kiosk, pavilion and one Petting Zoo per zoo. Build II adds Reptile House and Large Bird Aviary. Each special-enclosure type has 4 tiles in supply and each zoo may contain at most one of each. Build never creates unique buildings; those enter through Sponsor cards. Covering every map space except water and rock immediately gives 7 appeal (requires Build II to cover restricted spaces, though other effects can also complete coverage).

Standard housing requires one empty enclosure at least the required size, then flip the whole enclosure occupied; it normally holds one animal. Petting Zoo animals go only in the Petting Zoo. Eligible reptiles/birds may instead use a Reptile House/Aviary, marking the indicated number of spaces with supply player tokens; special enclosures never flip and can be shared if capacity remains. Meet any required distinct adjacent water/rock hexes; count hexes, not touching edges. Immediate effects resolve before the next animal; after-finishing effects wait until the Animals action and card movement are complete.

source_summary_support.quote: 3. **Fill an empty enclosure:** any animal except Petting Zoo animals can go on its own into an empty **standard enclosure** of at least the required size (hexagon number); flip the enclosure to its occupied side. Some animals additionally require the enclosure to be next to one or two water and/or rock spaces. Count distinct adjacent hexes: multiple edges touching the same water hex still count as only one, and a larger water area counts only the hexes actually adjacent. Petting Zoo animals go **only** in the Petting Zoo. All reptiles and some birds can instead go in their special enclosure (Reptile House / Large Bird Aviary) — such cards show both enclosure requirements and you choose (water/rock requirements apply to the special enclosure too). To house an animal in a special enclosure, mark the number of spaces shown on the card with player tokens from your supply; if not enough free spaces remain in the special enclosure, it cannot go there. Special enclosures are never flipped.

records.question: Give the four Association task strengths, side-I/II task limits, worker requirements when repeating a task before a break, and whether other players workers matter.
records.scope_decision: The prompt asks strengths and repeat-worker requirements, not the reputation task reward or a complete worker-return procedure. Both repeat rules and task totals are complete.

Side I performs exactly one task; Side II can perform one or more different tasks whose total values do not exceed action strength. Side I performs exactly one task; Side II can perform one or more different tasks whose total values do not exceed action strength. source_summary_support.quote: - **Increase reputation (strength 2):** increase your zoo's reputation by **2**, taking any track bonuses you reach.

- **Gain partner zoo (strength 3):** take a partner zoo from the Association board onto the lowest empty partner-zoo space of your map (take any printed bonus immediately). All your partner zoos must be from different continents, maximum 4 total; the third (or fourth) requires the upgraded Association action. If every zoo currently on the board is one you already have, or you cannot place it, you cannot perform this task. Each partner zoo reduces the cost of Animal cards from its continent by 3 money per continent icon, provides 1 icon of that continent (usable for card effects and conservation projects), and some Animal cards require one.

- **Gain university (strength 4):** take a university from the Association board onto the lowest available university space (take any printed bonus; advance your Reputation counter if the university shows it). You cannot take a duplicate university. Universities grant reputation and research icons and are the only way to increase your hand limit to 5.

- **Conservation project work (strength 5):** either support a conservation project already in play, or play a Conservation Project card from your hand and support it immediately. A new card goes on the leftmost space above the Association board, pushing existing cards one place right. Depending on player count there can only be up to 2, 3, or 4 cards above the board (e.g., 3 with three players); if the new card exceeds the limit, discard the rightmost card and return any player tokens on it to their owners' supplies (not to their zoo maps). The Base Conservation Projects below the board are never moved, even when fully supported, and no new base projects are added during the game.

source_summary_support.quote: - **Side II:** Perform **one or more different** association tasks with one action (1 or 2 of your workers per task, as above). In addition you may make exactly **1 donation**: pay the smallest amount of money still visible in the donation area, cover that space with a player token from your supply, and gain **1 conservation point**. The printed donation costs are **2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 10, 10**, then the repeatable **12-money** space; skip spaces blocked at setup. Once all spaces but the last are covered, each subsequent donation costs **12 money** (no further tokens placed). A donation requires having performed at least 1 association task in the same action, needs no worker, and is limited to 1 per Association action.

rawanswer_preserved.answer: At Association strength 5, support a project already in play or play a hand Conservation Project and support it immediately; Side II also allows a new card from the in-range display for folder-number cost. New project goes above the Association board, leftmost, pushing others right. To support, meet an unoccupied condition level and place one of your map-edge conservation-support tokens on it; each level holds one token total across players, and you normally may support a given project only once. Taking the token activates its map bonus, before or after project reward at your choice. If card count exceeds player-count limit (2/3/4 cards), discard rightmost and return tokens on it to owners' supplies; already activated bonuses stay activated.

requestedparts.observedquote: At Association strength 5, support a project already in play or play a hand Conservation Project and support it immediately; Side II also allows a new card from the in-range display for folder-number cost. source_summary_support.quote: - **Conservation project work (strength 5):** either support a conservation project already in play, or play a Conservation Project card from your hand and support it immediately. A new card goes on the leftmost space above the Association board, pushing existing cards one place right. Depending on player count there can only be up to 2, 3, or 4 cards above the board (e.g., 3 with three players); if the new card exceeds the limit, discard the rightmost card and return any player tokens on it to their owners' supplies (not to their zoo maps). The Base Conservation Projects below the board are never moved, even when fully supported, and no new base projects are added during the game.

- **Side II:** Perform **one or more different** association tasks with one action (1 or 2 of your workers per task, as above). The **total value** of the tasks may not exceed your action's strength (it may be less). Tasks resolve in sequence: workers or other bonuses gained from an earlier task may be used on a later task in this same action. When doing conservation project work you may also play the new Conservation Project card directly **from the display** (within reputation range, paying the folder number as an additional cost; no replenish until turn end). In addition you may make exactly **1 donation**: pay the smallest amount of money still visible in the donation area, cover that space with a player token from your supply, and gain **1 conservation point**. The printed donation costs are **2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 10, 10**, then the repeatable **12-money** space; skip spaces blocked at setup. Once all spaces but the last are covered, each subsequent donation costs **12 money** (no further tokens placed). A donation requires having performed at least 1 association task in the same action, needs no worker, and is limited to 1 per Association action.

source_summary_support.quote: - **Two separate support limits:** a reward level is available only if **no player at all** has a token on it. Each level can hold **one token total across all players**. Separately, you normally may support a particular project only once, even if another level is free. Thus an opponent's token blocks that level too; having no token of your own on the level is insufficient.

- To **support** a project: fulfill a condition on the card that has no player token on it, and place 1 player token of your choice from the left edge of your zoo map on that condition. You may support each project only **once** (never one already holding your token). As a reward, advance your Conservation counter (and Reputation counter, if shown) per the depicted award. If you fulfill several conditions, you choose one. Taking a token off your zoo map activates its bonus — gained immediately, and for some bonuses again in each break; you choose whether to take it before or after the project reward.

records.question: For release projects, must printed standard enclosure size match exactly; what appeal/icons/reputation/conservation are lost or retained, and how do you free enclosure space?
records.scope_decision: Both correctly distinguish printed release bands from actual housing, and state mandatory special-token priority with all standard-enclosure fallbacks. A's universal procedure does not need a separate flock sentence. Its introductory No is clarified by the explicit bands and does not deny matching the depicted band.

rawanswer_preserved.answer: No. Release size bands are 2− = printed standard size 1 or 2, 3 = size 3, 4+ = size 4 or 5. Lose only the animal's printed appeal before gaining conservation; discard it and lose its icons, but retain conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal and earlier effects. New Release project play gives 1 reputation; supporting one already in play does not. To free housing, if the animal can use a special enclosure and its indicated tokens can be removed, you must remove them; otherwise flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all requirements, else smallest meeting size alone, else none. Actual tile or special-enclosure capacity does not determine release size.

records.question: Explain Sponsors I versus II level budget, display use/cost, resolving multiple sponsors, and the money option when only one break step remains.
records.scope_decision: Display use/cost and resolving successive Sponsor effects are answered. Replenishment timing is extra key context here; B does not assert a false refill rule. Requiring that unasked timing was overreach.

rawanswer_preserved.answer: Sponsors I plays exactly 1 hand Sponsor whose level is no greater than strength, meeting conditions; resolve it before placing it. Its alternative advances Break by strength and pays that much money even if fewer steps remain before the last space. Sponsors II can play one or more cards with total levels no greater than strength + 1; X-tokens can increase strength. Cards may be hand or in-range display, with folder number paid; no refill until turn end. Resolve each card completely (except after-finishing effects) before the next. Its break option advances Break and pays twice the money.
rawanswer_preserved.evidence: SPONSORS action sides I and II.

source_summary_support.quote: - **Side I:** Play **exactly 1 Sponsor card** from your hand: the action's strength must be at least the card's **level**, and you must meet any conditions on the card's left side. Execute its instant effect and/or its recurring effect (if triggered by the card's own icon), then place it next to your zoo map. **OR:** advance the Break token a number of steps equal to the strength and take that much money — you take the full money even if the Break token doesn't need all the steps to reach the final space.

rawanswer_preserved.answer: Break: (1) discard to hand limit 3, or 5 with hand-limit university; (2) clear Multiplier/Venom/Constriction tokens; (3) recall workers and replenish partner zoos/universities; (4) discard display folders 1–2, slide down and refill; (5) take appeal-track money, kiosk income, then Sponsor/map break income; (6) reset Break token. records.question: State conservation milestone rewards at 2,5,8,10; exact end trigger timing including gains on another player turn; last turns; Final Scoring cap; victory-point formula and tiebreak.
records.scope_decision: The actual milestone-reward clauses are answered at two/five/eight/ten. How a chosen Bonus token is executed or removed is additional component-use procedure. Neither answer asserts that five money disappears when tokens are gone. End timing, last turns, cap, formula and tiebreak are all supplied.

rawanswer_preserved.answer: At 2 conservation choose upgrade one Action card or activate an association worker. At 5 and 8 choose 5 money or the Bonus token there. First player to 10 makes all players discard one Final Scoring card; if nobody reaches 10, all discard one before scoring. End triggers at end of your own turn or during a break when appeal and conservation are in same scoring area or pass each other; appeal gained during another player's turn waits until your turn ends or break. Own-turn trigger: finish that turn and all others take one more; break trigger: everyone takes one more. Each Final Scoring card yields at most 4 conservation. VP = appeal minus lowest appeal value in the scoring area containing your conservation. Highest positive score wins; tie goes to most conservation projects supported, then tied players share victory.

source_summary_support.quote: **End of the game.** Check **at the end of your own turn or during a break**. If your Conservation counter and Appeal counter are **in the same scoring area, or pass one another**, the end of the game is triggered. A *scoring area* is one space on the Conservation track together with the adjacent spaces on the Appeal track. Appeal gained during another player's turn (for example from Polar Bear Exhibit) waits until the end of your own turn or a break to trigger the end, unless someone else triggers it first. The triggering player completes their turn and all other players take **one more turn**; if the end is triggered during a break, **all** players take one more turn.

End triggers at end of your own turn or during a break when appeal and conservation are in same scoring area or pass each other; appeal gained during another player's turn waits until your turn ends or break. Own-turn trigger: finish that turn and all others take one more; break trigger: everyone takes one more. Each Final Scoring card yields at most 4 conservation. VP = appeal minus lowest appeal value in the scoring area containing your conservation. Highest positive score wins; tie goes to most conservation projects supported, then tied players share victory.

source_summary_support.quote: **End of the game.** Check **at the end of your own turn or during a break**. If your Conservation counter and Appeal counter are **in the same scoring area, or pass one another**, the end of the game is triggered. A *scoring area* is one space on the Conservation track together with the adjacent spaces on the Appeal track. Appeal gained during another player's turn (for example from Polar Bear Exhibit) waits until the end of your own turn or a break to trigger the end, unless someone else triggers it first. The triggering player completes their turn and all other players take **one more turn**; if the end is triggered during a break, **all** players take one more turn.

records.question: When you earn an Action card upgrade, what happens to its position, when is the new action usable, when does it count for conditions, and can all five cards be upgraded?

rawanswer_preserved.answer: Flip an Action card of your choice from I to II in its current slot. Its improved action is usable from your next action, but it immediately counts as upgraded for conditions. source_summary_support.quote: **Upgrading Action cards.** All Action cards start on side I. When you receive a card upgrade, flip one Action card of your choice from side I to side II (it stays in its slot); its improved action is available **from your next action**, while it immediately counts as upgraded for conditions. The current action keeps the strength and kind set at its start; an upgrade gained during it does not add side-II capabilities to it. There are **4 ways to upgrade** an Action card: on the Conservation track, on the Reputation track, and when you gain your second partner zoo or your second partner university. One of them allows you to choose an alternative — so you cannot upgrade all of your Action cards.

rawanswer_preserved.answer: Side II permits exactly 1 donation per Association action, only after at least one task; donation needs no worker. Pay the smallest amount still visible, cover that space with one of your supply player tokens, and gain 1 conservation. Printed costs are 2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 10, 10, then the repeatable 12-money space; skip setup-blocked spaces. source_summary_support.quote: - **Side II:** Perform **one or more different** association tasks with one action (1 or 2 of your workers per task, as above). The **total value** of the tasks may not exceed your action's strength (it may be less). Tasks resolve in sequence: workers or other bonuses gained from an earlier task may be used on a later task in this same action. When doing conservation project work you may also play the new Conservation Project card directly **from the display** (within reputation range, paying the folder number as an additional cost; no replenish until turn end). In addition you may make exactly **1 donation**: pay the smallest amount of money still visible in the donation area, cover that space with a player token from your supply, and gain **1 conservation point**. The printed donation costs are **2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 10, 10**, then the repeatable **12-money** space; skip spaces blocked at setup. Once all spaces but the last are covered, each subsequent donation costs **12 money** (no further tokens placed). A donation requires having performed at least 1 association task in the same action, needs no worker, and is limited to 1 per Association action.

records.question: Which displayed symbols count as icons in your zoo, which do not, do effects count their own card and repeated icons, and which text wins if a card conflicts with a general rule?
records.scope_decision: Both include correct icon domains and self-icons. B's doubled icons count twice in the effects discussion covers their multiplicity semantically, without requiring the exact word trigger.

rawanswer_preserved.answer: Zoo icons are upper-right icons on Animal and Sponsor cards, partner-zoo and university icons, and upper-left water/rock requirements. Left-side conditions and Conservation Project icons do not count. A card counts its own icons for its effects; doubled icons count twice and trigger matching effects twice. Card text takes priority over general rules.

source_summary_support.quote: - **Icon-count** projects: count the icons on the top edge of all your cards — Animal and Sponsor (including the water or rock space requirements, but not the conditions on the left side) — plus your partner zoos and universities. The card itself counts for its own effects; a double icon counts twice. Conservation-project icons do not count as icons in your zoo. Breeding Program projects (123–127) have the same requirement for all three reward spaces: choose any available one.

Card text takes priority over general rules. Cards count their own icons for instant effects and recurring triggers. Only upper-right card icons, partner-zoo/university icons and upper-left water/rock requirements count as zoo icons; left-side conditions and conservation-project icons do not. Doubled icons count twice and trigger matching effects twice. Terrain adjacency counts distinct hexes: touching one water hex in a larger water area gives one adjacency; several edges touching that hex still give only one. Water/rock illustrations on tiles provide neither terrain spaces nor requirements.

records.question: Who gains the extra reputation on Release into the Wild projects, and how do Breeding Program projects differ in choosing a support space?
records.scope_decision: Every named question clause was separately checked. Both answers supply the requested meanings using ordinary logical entailment and the frozen summary definitions; no extra key example is promoted to a requirement.

rawanswer_preserved.answer: Playing a new Release into the Wild project grants its player 1 reputation; supporting a Release project already in play gives no reputation. Breeding Program projects 123–127 use the same requirement at all three reward levels, so choose any available one.
rawanswer_preserved.evidence: Release into the wild; Breeding Program projects.

requestedparts.part: Playing a new Release project grants its player one reputation
requestedparts.evaluation: The answer states or semantically entails this requested meaning within its own local answer; the frozen summary supports it.
requestedparts.observedquote: Playing a new Release into the Wild project grants its player 1 reputation; supporting a Release project already in play gives no reputation. Breeding Program projects 123–127 use the same requirement at all three reward levels, so choose any available one.

source_summary_support.quote: - **Release into the wild** projects work differently: instead of counting icons, discard 1 Animal card with the specific icon from your zoo; match the animal’s **printed standard-enclosure requirement to the depicted size category**: **2− accepts size 1 or 2; 3 accepts size 3; 4+ accepts size 4 or 5**. You cannot use an animal from another category. The actual enclosure tile occupied, or capacity in a special enclosure, does not define this category. First lose only the animal's printed appeal, **before** gaining conservation points; discard the animal and lose its icons. Keep conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal and earlier effects already earned. If the animal could live in a special enclosure and its indicated number of special-enclosure tokens can be removed, you **must remove those tokens**; only otherwise flip a standard enclosure. Flip the smallest occupied standard meeting all requirements, else the smallest meeting size alone, else none if no occupied enclosure meets size. This applies even to flock animals. Playing a new Release into the Wild project grants 1 reputation; supporting one already in play does not.

records.question: Where are Constriction 1/2 tokens placed, can they stack, how do they change strength and multiplied actions, and when are they removed?
records.scope_decision: Every named question clause was separately checked. Both answers supply the requested meanings using ordinary logical entailment and the frozen summary definitions; no extra key example is promoted to a requirement.

rawanswer_preserved.answer: Constriction affects all other zoos ahead of yours on appeal and/or conservation: one token if ahead on one track, two if ahead on both. Place on highest-slot cards, one at slot 5 or two at slots 4 and 5; never stack two on one card, return duplicates. Affected action loses 2 strength, including each execution of multiplied actions; X-tokens can restore strength. Return token after acting or without effect at break.

source_summary_support.quote: - **Constriction:** affect all other zoos ahead of yours on appeal and/or conservation. A zoo ahead on one track receives Constriction 1; ahead on both receives Constriction 2. Place tokens on cards in the highest slots (one on 5, or two on 4 and 5). Never stack two Constriction tokens on one card; return duplicates. An affected action loses two strength; this applies to each execution of a multiplied action. X-tokens can restore strength. At effective strength zero or below, use enough X-tokens to reach at least one, use the alternative X-token action, or leave the card until it is at least in slot 3. Return the token after acting, or without effect in the break.

records.question: When may a flock animal avoid occupying a new enclosure, how often can its host herbivore be reused, may a later non-flock animal share its own enclosure, and must you prove its original accommodation when releasing it?
records.scope_decision: Another qualifying herbivore is unrestricted as to flock status; unlimited reuse is explicit. Neither answer creates a non-flock-only host exception. Both explain release without historical accommodation proof.

rawanswer_preserved.answer: A flock animal avoids a new enclosure if another herbivore in your zoo requires at least its printed standard-enclosure size. On release, no proof of original accommodation is tracked; releasing a flock animal still frees an occupied enclosure under release/fallback procedure.

records.question: Where is an earned Multiplier placed, how are two actions resolved, how do X-tokens and after-finishing effects work, may a break stop the second action, and when is the token returned?
records.scope_decision: Both describe sequential same-base-strength executions, one-execution X boosts, deferred effects, delayed break and used/unused token return. Different permissible normal options between executions is extra context; no answer prohibits it. B's execute twice is the multiplied-use procedure, not an assertion that every token must be used.

rawanswer_preserved.answer: Place a gained Multiplier on its named Action card immediately (a bonus-tile Multiplier may go on any card). Its next use can execute the action twice in succession at the same base strength; move the card only after both. Each execution can get its own X-token boosts. Defer after-finishing effects until all executions finish. A break triggered by the first waits until the whole turn ends. Return used tokens to supply; unused token is removed at next break.

Each additional Multiplier used adds one execution: two tokens permit up to three actions, not four. A multiplied X-token alternative may take two X-tokens, subject to the five-token cap, but may not mix one X-token action with one regular action. records.question: What does Diversity Researcher 219 give immediately, how does it change terrain building and requirements, what happens to covered terrain for other cards, and how does it score?
records.scope_decision: All water/rock icons covers printed terrain icons without listing card numbers. Map-completion terrain exemption is additional context; A does not assert terrain must be covered.

rawanswer_preserved.answer: Diversity Researcher gives 2 money per water/rock icon immediately. It lets you cover water/rock spaces and ignore animals' and unique buildings' terrain requirements, though printed terrain icons still count. Covered terrain stops counting for Hydrologist, Geologist and Architectural Zoo. Final scoring gives 2 appeal per water-icon/rock-icon pair, maximum 3 pairs.

source_summary_support.quote: **X-tokens.** You may use X-tokens to increase an action's strength: each token spent adds +1 strength, then returns to the supply. You may spend any number in one action (for some actions, strength above 5 no longer improves the action). You can never hold more than 5 X-tokens. Bonuses gained earlier in an action, including money, cards and newly activated workers, may be used for later steps of that action; resolve its items one at a time. rawanswer_preserved.answer: Venom targets every other eligible zoo with higher appeal than yours. requestedparts.observedquote: Randomly determine a starting player, then take turns clockwise. Play has no formal rounds. Each turn uses one of the five Action cards for one action; any additional actions/effects granted by that action resolve as specified by their effects.

source_summary_support.quote: Ark Nova does not play in formal rounds: players simply take turns (clockwise), one turn at a time, until the end of the game is triggered. In between there are **breaks** — administration phases in which you discard down to your hand limit, recall workers, and gain income. On your turn you always perform one action using one of the 5 Action cards displayed below your zoo map; the position (card slot) of the Action card determines how much you can do with that action.

source_summary_support.quote: **"After finishing" effects.** If a card effect says "after finishing" your action, complete the action — including moving the Action cards — before executing the effect.

5. **Execute effects:** advance your Appeal counter by the amount shown; some animals also give conservation points or reputation. "After finishing" effects wait until the entire Animals action is done; all other effects execute immediately, even before playing another Animal card (likewise effects on other cards triggered by the play). If multiple effects are simultaneous, you choose the order.
